prompts.text: What first taught you that two friends can need very different kinds of personal space?
Tell me about someone respecting your need for time alone without taking it personally.
Discuss how much contact feels natural or talk about which topics need more privacy?
A friend likes spontaneous visitors but you prefer advance notice. How could you agree on a routine?
Comfort with closeness is shaped by more than how long two people have known each other.
The ability to say no without giving a detailed reason can strengthen a friendship.
Which boundary do you understand better now than you did as a teenager?
Recall a time you misread a friend's silence and later learnt what they needed.
A friend asks you to keep a personal update confidential. What would you clarify about who already knows?
Talk about your social limits upfront or revisit them naturally as a friendship develops?
What makes a person's listening style feel comforting when you need to explain something complicated?
Describe someone helping you understand yourself by asking an unexpected question.
Have a friend paraphrase what they heard or give you time to finish without interruption?
Two friends have different recollections of the same conversation. How might they check the facts together?
People often remember how a conversation made them feel more clearly than the exact words spoken.
Listening well sometimes means admitting you don't have an answer.
What question do you wish friends would ask before offering advice about your decisions?
Recall a friend who was curious about your reasoning even though they disagreed with your conclusion.
A conversation begins to feel like a debate when one person wants empathy. What might help reset it?
Discuss a misunderstanding right away or agree to return when everyone has had time to reflect?
What has friendship taught you about people whose faith or beliefs differ from yours?
Tell me about being invited to observe a tradition and learning why it mattered to someone.
Understand a friend's meaningful annual observance or learn about the everyday values behind their practices?
A close friend has an important celebration unfamiliar to your household. What questions would help you support them?
People with different beliefs may share practical values that are easier to see through daily actions.
Respecting a belief doesn't require pretending you've never questioned it.
What kind of curiosity feels welcome when someone asks about your personal beliefs?
Recall discovering that a friend's view of a moral question was more nuanced than you assumed.
Two friends disagree about an important belief while planning a public event. How could they stay considerate?
Ask about what shaped someone's convictions or about how those convictions influence their daily routine?
How have friends influenced the way you handle personal setbacks?
Describe a friend whose persistence you admired during an unplanned change.
Discuss a lesson you've learnt from failure or a strength you've discovered in an unexpected situation?
A friend's business idea hasn't worked and they're considering another attempt. What would you want to understand first?
It's possible to admire a friend's courage while questioning a specific decision.
Friendship includes the freedom to respond to a setback differently from what others expect.
Which quality in a friend becomes most visible when life doesn't go as planned?
Recall seeing someone respond with patience to a disappointment they'd worked hard to avoid.
A friend wants to celebrate trying something difficult despite not succeeding. How would you help?
Hear how someone recovered from a setback or learn what motivated them to start in the first place?
What difference between your friends' cultures has encouraged you to reconsider a habit?
Tell me about participating in a celebration that felt unfamiliar but welcoming.
Compare traditions for honouring elders or ways different communities welcome new neighbours?
Your friends from several countries plan to host one shared meal. What would you ask each person to contribute?
Cultural differences often appear first in ordinary etiquette rather than formal ceremonies.
Interest in another culture is most useful when people remain free to explain it in their own words.
Which local saying becomes more meaningful after someone explains the story behind it?
Recall learning why a friend used a particular greeting in a specific setting.
A friend visits your hometown and notices a custom you've never thought about. How would you answer their questions?
Learn a traditional game from a friend's community or cook a dish with them and hear its history?
What makes a new member of an established friendship group feel genuinely included?
Describe seeing someone join a group and quietly change it for the better.
Ask newcomers what activities they'd enjoy or explain the group's existing traditions first?
Your friendship circle has an inside joke that leaves a recent arrival confused. How might you tell the story?
Groups often overlook how much background knowledge their conversations assume.
An inclusive group leaves room for its newest people to influence shared decisions.
What's a sign that one person in a group is struggling to find a comfortable role?
Recall a friend making sure another person received credit for an idea.
Several friends have different preferences about inviting partners to gatherings. What agreement could help?
Rotate who chooses activities or hold an open conversation when group habits stop working?
How do you decide whether a friend's difficult feedback is worth taking seriously?
Tell me about advice you resisted at first but appreciated after considering it.
Receive one carefully explained suggestion or several perspectives to compare independently?
A friend believes you're making a poor decision but hasn't been asked for input. How could they approach you?
Helpful feedback often depends as much on timing as on the insight itself.
You can appreciate someone's honesty without following their recommendation.
What has made you trust a friend's judgement on a subject they know well?
Recall a friend admitting they didn't know enough to advise you and helping you find someone who did.
Two trusted friends suggest opposite solutions to one problem. What would you ask them about their assumptions?
Discuss why someone gave you advice or ask them to help you evaluate the possible outcomes?
What would you want an old friend to understand about the person you've become?
Describe reconnecting after years apart and discovering a shared value you hadn't noticed before.
Compare the ambitions you had when you met or the lessons you value most now?
An old classmate remembers you mainly for a habit you've outgrown. How could you help them see the change?
Friends sometimes hold a picture of one another that belongs to a different period of life.
A long history together should make room for new versions of each person.
Which quality did you gain after leaving an environment where most of your friendships began?
Recall visiting a familiar place with a friend and noticing how differently you now see it.
Two friends who once shared everything develop very different priorities. What could they still build together?
Revisit a favourite memory or create a new experience that reflects who you are today?
Which friendship have you learnt the most from without seeing the person frequently?
Tell me about a former colleague or neighbour who unexpectedly became an important connection.
Stay connected through shared projects or through occasional unhurried conversations?
A friend moves to another city and neither person enjoys long calls. What alternative would feel natural?
Closeness can grow through reliability even when people spend little time together.
An occasional sincere conversation can mean more than frequent messages sent out of obligation.
Which small routine would help you reconnect with a friend after a demanding season of life?
Recall a short catch-up that helped you discover how much had changed for somebody.
You learn that a friend you rarely speak to has achieved something meaningful. How would you acknowledge it thoughtfully?
Plan a future visit together or exchange a few thoughtful questions over the next month?
What have your closest friends taught you about the kind of person you want to be?
Describe discovering a quality you admired in several people from different parts of your life.
Talk about an example of everyday integrity or a friendship lesson you hope to pass on?
A younger person asks why you stay close to a particular friend. Which story would best explain it?
The friendships people keep often reflect values they didn't consciously list when they first met.
A meaningful friendship doesn't have to be the most visible relationship in someone's life.
Which quality would you hope your friends use when describing you to someone new?
Recall a friend showing you how to respond generously when somebody made a mistake.
You and a friend decide to work on becoming more considerate people. What's a concrete habit you might practise?
Share the lesson that changed you most or thank someone for a quality you've learnt from them?
